subject: english-a
introduction: Writing frames and language rules for CSEC English A — summary, essay, grammar, and vocabulary strategies.

items.name: Find main points
items.formula: read twice; underline only what answers the question
items.notes: Omit examples, repetitions, adjectives, and figurative decoration.

items.name: Draft in your words
items.formula: one paragraph, ~120 words, no bullets, no intro/conclusion
items.notes: Link points with connectives (furthermore, however, consequently).

items.name: Length check
items.formula: count words and adjust — over/under limit loses marks
items.notes: Keep the original tense; never copy whole sentences if you can paraphrase.

items.name: PEEL paragraph
items.formula: Point → Evidence/Example → Explanation → Link
items.notes: One clear point per paragraph; link back to the question.

items.name: Expository essay frame
items.formula: intro (thesis) → 3 body paragraphs (PEEL) → conclusion (restate + insight)
items.notes: Thesis statement = your controlling idea in the opening paragraph.

items.name: Argument essay frame
items.formula: claim → reasons + evidence → counter-argument + rebuttal → conclusion
items.notes: Persuasive devices: rhetorical questions, statistics, emotive language, expert opinion.

items.name: Narrative arc
items.formula: exposition → rising action → climax → falling action → resolution
items.notes: Show, don't tell: dialogue, sensory detail, varied sentence lengths.

items.name: Descriptive toolkit
items.formula: simile, metaphor, personification, alliteration, onomatopoeia, hyperbole
items.notes: 'The wind whispered' (personification); 'like sunshine' (simile); 'eat a horse' (hyperbole).

items.name: Letter/email layout
items.formula: address + date → greeting → purpose → details → close ('Yours sincerely/faithfully')
items.notes: Formal vs informal register: no slang or contractions in formal letters.

items.name: Subject–verb agreement
items.formula: singular subject → singular verb: 'Each student HAS'; collective as unit → singular
items.notes: 'Neither of the boys IS present'; 'He DOES not' / 'He DOESN'T' (not 'don't').

items.name: Tense consistency
items.formula: stay in one tense unless the meaning shifts
items.notes: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing ('She is singing').

items.name: Apostrophes
items.formula: possession (Maria's book) vs contraction (don't = do not)
items.notes: Plurals never take apostrophes ('books', not 'book's').

items.name: Punctuation map
items.formula: full stop ends statements; ? for questions; ! for exclamations; : introduces; ; joins related clauses
items.notes: Comma after an intro phrase ('After dinner, we went home'); colon before lists/explanations.

items.name: Common confusions
items.formula: their/there/they're; to/too/two; affect/effect; complement/compliment
items.notes: Proofread backwards sentence by sentence to catch them.

items.name: Sentence types
items.formula: simple (1 clause); compound (2 independent + conjunction); complex (independent + dependent)
items.notes: Comma splice and run-on fixes: split, join with conjunction, or use a semicolon.

items.name: Context clues
items.formula: definition, synonym, antonym, example, or inference from surrounding text
items.notes: 'Ominous clouds' → threatening, from the storm context.

items.name: Word parts
items.formula: prefix (un-, anti-, inter-) + root + suffix (-less = without; -ology = study of)
items.notes: Transport = trans (across) + port (carry).

items.name: Synonym/antonym pairs
items.formula: meticulous/careful; diligent/hardworking; candid/honest; ambiguous/unclear
items.notes: Antonyms: expand/contract; ancient/modern; transparent/opaque; reluctant/willing.

items.name: Idioms & proverbs
items.formula: bite the bullet (face difficulty); break the ice (start conversation); eleventh hour (last moment)
items.notes: Once in a blue moon (rarely); actions speak louder than words (deeds matter).

items.name: Spelling demons
items.formula: double-check: necessary, embarrass, recommend, separate, occurrence, sincerely
items.notes: Sound it out by syllables; learn 'i before e except after c' limits.
